entries.title: Filesystem
entries.description: Reads and writes files in the directories you allow, so an agent can work with a project's contents directly instead of being told about them.

entries.title: Git
entries.description: Reads history, diffs and branches in a local repository, so an agent can see how the code got to its current state before changing it.

entries.title: GitHub
entries.description: Opens and updates issues and pull requests, and searches code across repositories, so review and triage happen without leaving the session.

env.name: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.help: A fine grained token scoped to the repositories you want reachable. You can sign in with OAuth instead, in which case leave this unset and remove the Authorization header.

entries.title: GitLab
entries.description: Works with issues, merge requests and pipelines on GitLab. Self managed instances use their own hostname, so change the URL to match yours.

entries.title: Sentry
entries.description: Pulls up issues, stack traces and releases, so an agent debugging a failure can read the actual error rather than guess at it.

entries.title: Playwright
entries.description: Drives a real browser to navigate, fill forms, click and screenshot, so an agent can check what a page actually does rather than what the markup suggests.

entries.title: Chrome DevTools
entries.description: Opens the console, network panel and performance trace of a live Chrome page, which is where front end bugs usually explain themselves.

entries.title: Context7
entries.description: Fetches documentation for the exact version of a library you depend on, which is the usual cure for confidently wrong API calls.

env.name: CONTEXT7_API_KEY
env.help: Optional key from context7.com/dashboard that raises the rate limit.

entries.title: Fetch
entries.description: Retrieves a URL and converts the page to clean markdown, so an agent can read a doc page without the navigation and the cookie banner.

entries.title: Sequential Thinking
entries.description: Breaks a hard problem into numbered thoughts the agent can revise as it goes, instead of committing to an answer in one pass.

entries.title: Time
entries.description: Answers what the time is and converts between zones, which a model cannot do reliably on its own.

entries.title: Everything
entries.description: A reference server that exercises every part of the protocol. Worth adding when you are debugging a client rather than building something.

entries.title: Memory
entries.description: A knowledge graph the agent writes to and reads back, so what it learns about you survives past the end of a conversation.

entries.title: PostgreSQL
entries.description: Runs SQL and reports on query plans and index health, so an agent can answer questions about real data instead of the schema alone.

env.name: DATABASE_URI
env.help: Connection string, for example postgresql://user:pass@host:5432/db. Point it at a read only role unless you mean to allow writes.

entries.title: SQLite
entries.description: Queries a local SQLite file. Community maintained: the server the protocol authors published has been archived.

entries.title: MongoDB
entries.description: Queries and manages MongoDB databases and Atlas clusters, including collections, indexes and aggregation.

entries.title: Redis
entries.description: Reads and writes keys, hashes, lists, sets and streams, so an agent can inspect what is actually cached right now.

env.name: REDIS_PWD
env.help: Only needed when auth is enabled and the password is not already part of the URL.

entries.title: Supabase
entries.description: Manages projects, runs SQL and reads schema and logs, so an agent can work on the backend and the app in the same session.

env.name: SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.help: A personal access token from your Supabase account settings.

entries.title: Railway
entries.description: Creates services, deploys them and reads logs and metrics, so shipping and diagnosing a deployment stay in one place.

entries.title: Vercel
entries.description: Inspects projects, deployments, domains and build logs, which is usually where a failed preview explains itself.

entries.title: Cloudflare
entries.description: Manages Workers, DNS records and account resources, and searches the Cloudflare documentation.

entries.title: AWS
entries.description: Calls AWS APIs and gives service specific guidance. This is the entry point to the AWS Labs family of servers.

env.name: AWS_PROFILE
env.help: Named profile from your AWS CLI credentials file.

entries.title: Kubernetes
entries.description: Lists and manages pods, deployments and logs, so an agent can find the crashing container without a shell.

env.name: KUBECONFIG
env.help: Path to your kubeconfig. Defaults to wherever kubectl already looks.

entries.title: Linear
entries.description: Creates, searches and updates issues and projects, so work an agent finishes can be recorded where the team already tracks it.

entries.title: Notion
entries.description: Searches, reads and edits pages and databases, which makes a Notion workspace usable as the source of truth an agent reads from.

entries.title: Slack
entries.description: Searches messages, reads channels and posts, so an agent can find the thread where a decision was actually made.

entries.title: Jira and Confluence
entries.description: Searches and updates Jira issues and Confluence pages on an Atlassian Cloud site.

entries.title: Asana
entries.description: Reads and updates tasks, projects and workflows in an Asana workspace.

entries.title: Figma
entries.description: Reads components, styles and layout from the file open in Figma, so generated code follows the design rather than approximating it. Needs the Figma desktop app running.

entries.title: Brave Search
entries.description: Runs live web, image and news searches, so an agent can check something that happened after its training data ended.

env.name: BRAVE_API_KEY
env.help: Key from the Brave Search API dashboard.

entries.title: Stripe
entries.description: Manages customers, payments, subscriptions and refunds, and searches the Stripe documentation.

entries.title: Zapier
entries.description: Triggers automations across the apps you have already connected to Zapier, which covers the long tail of services with no server of their own.
